deities: Goddess Mahalakshmi (main idol, with nine other forms/swarup of Mataji around her)
festivals: Diwali/Deepotsav (Dhanteras to Bhai Dooj) - the signature festival

history.period: Nearly 300 years old (c. 18th century; Diwali tradition traced to the era of Maharaja Ratan Singh Rathore)
history.summary: The Mahalaxmi Temple at Manak Chowk, Ratlam, is one of Madhya Pradesh's most unusual temples: during the five days of Deepotsav (Dhanteras to Bhai Dooj) it is decorated not with flowers but with currency notes (Rs 10 to Rs 500), gold and silver jewellery and diamonds offered by devotees - reportedly the only temple in India to stay so adorned for five consecutive days, with decoration values around Rs 2 crore, all returned to devotees as prasad afterwards. The tradition dates to the princely era: when Maharaja Ratan Singh Rathore founded Ratlam city (Lakshmi was the royal family's kuldevi), the royal household offered wealth at the temple for five days each Diwali for prosperity, health and public welfare, and devotees later took the kings' place. The temple is now government-owned and administered under the Court of Wards, with administration supervising the decoration period. The garbhagriha famously opens for extended darshan (about 120 continuous hours) during Diwali.

name: Mahalaxmi Temple
town_description: Ratlam is a historic Malwa-region city in western Madhya Pradesh; the temple stands in the bustling Manak Chowk market in the heart of the old city, surrounded by shops catering to devotees.

travel.airport: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport, Indore (~140 km) is the nearest commercial airport.
travel.railway: Ratlam Junction is the nearest major railway station (~3 km), a major Delhi-Mumbai junction.
travel.road: Manak Chowk is in central Ratlam; the market area is congested, so walking or auto-rickshaw is easiest during festivals.

visitor_information.best_time: Diwali/Deepotsav (Dhanteras to Bhai Dooj) to see the unique currency-and-jewellery decoration; Navratri for garba.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Remains open for roughly 120 continuous hours during the five Diwali days (verify exact annual schedule); regular hours not published in consulted sources (verify). The market location means heavy crowds - plan accordingly.
